probe.termination: Explicit stop exceeded the five-second cooperative grace; host terminated guest execution and reported stateName=failed.

runs.runtimeHostHashNote: The Run 13 executable was overwritten by the later bounded critical-section diagnostic build; a separate hash was not captured before replacement.
runs.observed: Exact TU2 image loaded (title update applied, effective SHA-1 b771b41caef2483549bfbc7d726be3eb56943f99). MainThread remained at 0x827AF6B8 with 637680 guest blocks across a 15-second sample interval. KeDelayExecutionThread traces for threads 3 and 11 show mode 1, alertable 1, STATUS_SUCCESS, relative -10000 100-ns units (1 ms); the delay implementation is not shown to be the cause. No first frame/present; explicit stop timed out and forced termination followed.

The exact TU2 image again loaded and executed without a guest trap, but MainThread remained at 0x827AF6B8 with 634598 guest blocks. Bounded critical-section traces show ordinary lock acquisition and a thread-11 wait/wake on object 0xB582EF00; the global trace cap was consumed before the main-thread stall site was captured. No first frame/present; forced termination followed.
Fresh targeted-probe build failed before loading the XEX because the content graph mount returned Failed to mount content graph. This run provides no evidence about the target callsite.

The same content graph mount failure reproduced under the restricted launch context. Elevated CTest later identified HostPathDevice canonicalization as AccessDenied for the restricted path; elevated probes mounted the same content successfully. This run provides no evidence about the target callsite.

Elevated launch resolved content mounting and loaded the exact TU2 image. MainThread progressed to 929485 guest blocks; thread 8 last reported PC was 0x827AF6B8. This PC alone did not establish a stall cause. No first frame/present.

Per-thread traces show threads 3, 8, 11, and 12 repeatedly acquired critical sections reached from 0x827AF6B8. One thread-11 contention on 0xB582EF00 registered, waited, and woke successfully. Guest threads collectively executed millions of blocks; the callsite is not supported as a permanent critical-section deadlock. No first frame/present.

The rebuilt host loaded and bound the same exact TU2 image (SHA-1 b771b41caef2483549bfbc7d726be3eb56943f99; SHA-256 EBDCBE683DB2F1C29AA43AC97E79492926C099B2EE253DB502CABCBEC133D52F), created its 1280x720 window, and ran until a documented graceful stop. Across 1,380 GPU-pump ticks, the GPU ring stayed unconfigured (base/capacity 0), pending IR stayed 0, and the front buffer stayed unset (base/generation 0); present was skipped each vsync. No guest trap. MainThread reached 442,287 guest blocks. This establishes that the immediate issue precedes GPU submission; it does not identify why guest startup has not reached graphics initialization.

followUpRuntimeTrace.callsiteAnalysis: Run24 supersedes the stale handoff/critical-section hypothesis: periodic PCs traversed several guest regions, and the focused 0x82C715D8..0x82C715EC path performs successful 1 ms/3 ms relative KeDelayExecutionThread calls. Sampled NtWaitForSingleObjectEx calls on other threads returned expected STATUS_TIMEOUT. No guest trap was reported, but there is still no first frame or Vd ring/front-buffer activity. The updated Vd service trace has compiled, but Run25 could not boot because HostPathDevice failed to mount content.

codeInspection.loop: At 0x8229CD84, r10 is set to r5-1, checked for zero, copied into CTR, then the 0x8229CDA8 loop stores zero bytes while decrementing CTR.
codeInspection.interpretation: The stable reported PC is consistent with execution inside a count-controlled guest loop. Available logs do not capture r5/CTR at loop entry, so they cannot distinguish a valid large operation from an invalid length or a runtime memory/performance problem. No loop semantics were changed.

critic.largestGap: The updated host compiles, but its targeted run cannot reach guest code because HostPathDevice fails to mount content under the available token; the desktop blocks UAC relaunch with Access denied. No run validates the Vd trace or first frame.
critic.nextAction: Run the exact-TU2 probe in an actually elevated Windows process, verify the Vd trace and host status, and inspect the resulting calls before changing service semantics.

run24.focusedTrace: Generated function at 0x82C71598 calls KeDelayExecutionThread from 0x82C715E8. Run24 logs show successful relative 1 ms and 3 ms delays (status 0); sampled NtWaitForSingleObjectEx calls on other guest threads returned expected timeout 0x102. This disproves a permanent delay/critical-section interpretation but does not explain why Vd graphics services have not run.
